title: A Thorn for the Wolf Again
premise: Bram Almeida, a royal food-taster whose body is a ledger of poisons survived, secretly keeps the accounts of the Guild of Impossible Things—traders in bottled memories, borrowed years, and names that shouldn't exist. When a mute child arrives at her door speaking a language older than any kingdom, Bram discovers the girl is a living key: the unbinding word for the thing that has worn the king's crown for thirty years. To reach the throne room, Bram must trade away pieces of herself through the Guild's ledgers—her immunity, her memories of found family, finally her own name—while the crown-thing hunts the child through everyone Bram loves. In the end she unbinds the king at the cost of being forgotten by everyone she saved, until the child, now grown and keeper of the ledgers, writes Bram's name back into the world.
about_author: Coral Iversen is a former archivist who claims she left the profession after cataloguing a box of letters addressed to people who had never been born. She writes fantasy about paperwork, poison, and the quiet heroism of people who keep records.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. She tastes the king's breakfast, survives a subtle arsenic lacing, and returns to her rooms above the Guild counting house to balance impossible ledgers. Establishes her double life and her numb pride in a body built for survival. Emotional beat: lonely competence.

chapters.title: Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A tour of the Guild's back office: vials of borrowed courage, a jar of last words, debts written in hair. Her mentor Odile Voss explains the Guild serves whoever pays, never asks why. Beat: uneasy complicity.

chapters.title: The Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, night. A girl of eight appears in the snow, speaking a language no scholar knows—and the ledger opens itself to record her arrival before Bram touches the pen. Beat: dread wrapped in wonder.

chapters.title: Words Older Than Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The Guild's oldest member, a mummified broker called Ninepence, wakes to hear the child and identifies the tongue as First Speech—the language in which binding oaths were originally sworn. Beat: the past waking up hungry.

chapters.title: What the Crown Remembers
chapters.summary: Bram's POV at court. Serving the king's wine, she notices he answers questions a half-second before they're asked, and his shadow moves wrong. She begins keeping a private ledger of royal anomalies. Beat: creeping horror beneath ceremony.

chapters.title: A Debt Paid in Immunity
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. To buy the child safe passage from Guild informants, Bram trades thirty years of accumulated poison-immunity to the Guild's stores. She will taste again as an ordinary woman now. Beat: sacrifice disguised as bookkeeping.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Won't Speak
chapters.summary: Child's POV, rendered in close third. The girl, Wren, remembers only fragments: a tower, a burning oath, a voice saying 'carry it until someone worthy reads you.' She trusts Bram because Bram smells of swallowed deaths. Beat: fragile attachment.

chapters.title: Ninepence Names the Enemy
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Ninepence reveals the crown holds a bound thing—an oath-eater called the Hollow King—that consumed the real monarch decades ago and rules by wearing his shape. Only First Speech can unbind it. Beat: stakes crystallize.

chapters.title: The Guild Sells Both Sides
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A court chamberlain buys a memory-extraction from the Guild; Bram recognizes the extracted memory as Wren's face. The enemy is shopping. Beat: betrayal by institution.

chapters.title: First Poison Without Armor
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Back at court without her immunity, Bram must identify poison by wit alone and nearly dies covering for a paranoid princess. Odile saves her with an antidote priced against Bram's future labor. Beat: vulnerability made physical.

chapters.title: Wren Reads the Ledger
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Left alone with the master ledger, Wren touches a page and the First Speech letters rearrange into words she can read aloud—one syllable makes a candle gutter and a debt vanish. Beat: the key revealed.

chapters.title: The Princess Who Suspects
chapters.summary: Princess Isolde's POV. The king's daughter has spent years mapping her father's wrongness; she confronts Bram, having traced the Guild purchases. Uneasy alliance forms over shared evidence. Beat: two watchers recognizing each other.

chapters.title: A Name Withdrawn from Circulation
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. To erase Wren from Guild records, Bram withdraws her own name as collateral—if she fails her contract, she'll be unwritten. Odile warns her the Guild always collects. Beat: love priced in identity.

chapters.title: The Hunt Begins
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. Crown agents raid the Guild quarter; Ninepence burns rather than talk; Odile smuggles Bram and Wren into the undercity. Beat: flight, grief, momentum.

chapters.title: Undercity of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Hiding among Guild debtors who live on traded time, Bram learns some gave decades for children, causes, mistakes—a gallery of survival's price. Beat: compassion deepening theme.

chapters.title: What Wren Carries
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Under stress, Wren speaks a full sentence of First Speech and the room's bindings loosen—locks open, a chained debtor walks free. She is not just a key; she is a living unbinding. Beat: power and terror.

chapters.title: Isolde's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. She finds her true father's hidden testament: he bound the Hollow King deliberately, trading himself to stop a war, believing no one should hold absolute power—including him. Beat: tragic revelation reframing the villain.

chapters.title: The Offer from the Throne
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The Hollow King summons Bram, courteous and terrible, offering to restore her name, her immunity, and Wren's safety if she surrenders the child. It speaks in the voices of everyone Bram has lost. Beat: temptation with teeth.

chapters.title: Refusal and Reckoning
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram refuses, and the Hollow King unmakes her court position, blackening her name—she is now a traitor with a price on her head. Beat: the cost of loyalty to truth over survival.

chapters.title: Odile's Ledger Balanced
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile reveals she was the one who sold the original binding to the young king thirty years ago; she has been managing her guilt through the Guild ever since. She gives Bram the binding's original terms. Beat: confession as turning point.

chapters.title: The Terms of Binding
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Studying the old contract, Bram learns the binding requires a willing anchor—Wren was born into the oath-line as failsafe. Unbinding needs three things: the word, the witness, the willingness of the bound. Beat: plan assembled from wreckage.

chapters.title: Midnight Market
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV chapter. The fugitives barter in the black market for a witness qualified to stand before a crown: a priestess excommunicated for remembering too much. Beat: found family recruiting its strangest member.

chapters.title: The Priestess Who Remembered
chapters.summary: Mother Cassia's POV. She recalls officiating the king's coronation and hearing something answer from inside the crown. She agrees to witness, knowing witnesses to unbindings historically die. Beat: courage without guarantee.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Weir Gate
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A debtor they trusted sells their route to the crown; the party scatters; Cassia is captured. Bram chooses to go back for her against all sense. Beat: loyalty tested and proven costly.

chapters.title: Interrogation of the Witness
chapters.summary: Cassia's POV. In the palace cells, the Hollow King tries to eat her memories; her faith acts as grit in the mechanism. She stalls, learning it fears one thing: being witnessed truly. Beat: resistance as insight.

chapters.title: The Half-Ledger Gambit
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram breaks into the Guild vault to recover the original binding contract, trading her remaining memories of her childhood home to bypass the wards. She no longer remembers why she became a taster. Beat: hollowing out for the mission.

chapters.title: What I Cannot Remember
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, elegiac. Reading her own old journals like a stranger's, Bram reconstructs her motives from evidence. Wren quietly re-teaches her who she was. Beat: found family rebuilding what was sold.

chapters.title: Isolde Opens the Gates
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Using her evidence of the king's wrongness, Isolde turns the palace guard's captain, opening a path for the unbinding rite on solstice night when the crown's power thins. Beat: allies converging.

chapters.title: Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: Quiet ensemble chapter. The company shares a last meal—Bram cooks, tasting nothing, trusting her craft. Each character names what they're afraid to lose. Beat: stillness before storm, love made explicit.

chapters.title: The Long Corridor
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The infiltration begins; guards who owe Isolde look away; the Hollow King's voice follows them through the walls, offering each companion their heart's desire. Beat: gauntlet of temptations.

chapters.title: Cassia Freed
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren speaks her first deliberate sentence of First Speech to unlock Cassia's cell, and the palace's older bindings shudder. The Hollow King now knows exactly where they are. Beat: the key turns.

chapters.title: Throne Room of the Hollow King
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Confrontation: the thing in the crown drops the king's shape, revealing a beautiful absence. It argues its case—it ended a war, it has kept peace for thirty years. Beat: the villain almost wins rhetorically.

chapters.title: The Willingness of the Bound
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. The final term surfaces: the real king, fragmentary inside the binding, must consent to end. Through Cassia's rites, Isolde speaks with her father's remnant and receives his yes. Beat: grief and release entwined.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Wren speaks the word, Cassia witnesses, the king consents—but the Hollow King seizes Bram as counterweight, demanding a soul of equal weight. Bram offers her name, freely given, completing her old collateral. Beat: climax, sacrifice consummated.

chapters.title: The Empty Crown
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The thing unravels; the true king's body crumbles to dust mid-blessing; the crown falls inert. Bram collapses, and no one in the room can recall who she is. Beat: victory and erasure in the same breath.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Saved Kingdom
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Regency established, reforms begun—but a gap sits at every table where someone should be. Wren refuses to accept the loss. Beat: mourning with a stubborn spine.

chapters.title: The Ledger Keeper
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, years later. Now grown, Wren keeps the Guild's ledgers and searches every page for a way to write a person back. She finds the clause Bram once signed: names withdrawn may be re-entered by a willing debtor. Beat: hope through fine print.

chapters.title: Re-entered into the World
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren pays the price—her fluency in First Speech, her connection to the old magic—and writes Bram's name back. In a doorway in the city, a woman tastes the air, remembering everything at once. Beat: restoration earned, not gifted.

chapters.title: A Thorn for the Wolf Again
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Reunion: imperfect, tearful, real. Bram declines a return to court, choosing instead to co-keep the ledgers with Wren and Odile, guarding the Guild against its own worst habits. Beat: home redefined.

chapters.title: Closing Entries
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, coda. Balancing the final page, Bram records the whole affair in plain language and closes the book on a line she'll repeat forever: some things are survived, some are paid for, and the difference is who stood beside you. Beat: thematic resolution, warm and clear-eyed.
